No. With the vitest 5.0.3 installed here, Vitest only looks for a config file in the root directory, which is the current working directory unless you pass `--root`. It doesn't walk up into parent folders. The installed code shows this: `findConfigFile` in `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DpLw24bj.js:14267` only checks `root/<config name>`, and if nothing is there it returns `false` so Vite won't search either.

Older Vitest versions did search parent directories, so a setup that relied on that can quietly run with no config, and nothing will error. From a subfolder, pass the config explicitly with `vitest --config ../vitest.config.ts`, or set `--root` to the folder that contains it.
